attributes.VIOLATION_DESCRIPTION: Proper Cold Holding temperature(41øF/45øF)
attributes.V_MEMO:
Person in charge stated it is facility policy not to insert the probe thermometer into any foods as they will have to be discarded even if the thermometer is properly sanitized. Milk is poured into a container for temperature checks (acceptable), but a milk container was observed at 44°F. attributes.VIOLATION_DESCRIPTION: Proper Hot Holding temperature(135øF)
attributes.V_MEMO:
Observation:

attributes.NAME: EGGSQUISITE CAFE
attributes.VIOLATION_DESCRIPTION: Physical Facilities Installed, Maintained, and Clean
attributes.V_MEMO:
I observed on page 5, that the room schedule generally meets the required construction standards for health. However, on page 11, in the restroom, I noticed that black vinyl cove was installed instead of the specified ceramic cove. Please ensure that the room schedule specifications are followed as indicated on the page.

Additionally, I did not observe a designated dry storage area for dry goods. Please ensure that a storage area is added or designated if one has not yet been assigned. It is important that the storage area be sized adequately to accommodate the amount of dry goods that will be stored, depending on the number of days between deliveries, to ensure proper organization, accessibility, and compliance with food safety standards.



In the following information, I will provide specific construction standards for your reference.

 Please see below:

Floor Requirements:

Food preparation, tableware and utensil washing, customer service areas (including buffets), and toilet rooms must have quarry or ceramic tile floors with epoxy-containing, acid-resistant grout.Floors must have a covered floor-wall interface of at least four (4) inches in height, constructed of quarry or ceramic tile.
Dry storage rooms and areas around mop sinks must have sealed concrete or vinyl composition tile (VCT) floors. Floor-wall interface must include four (4) inch vinyl base coving when floor is concrete or VCT tile.

Wall Requirements:

Food preparation, tableware and utensil washing, and customer service areas (including self-service beverage areas) must have walls constructed of FRP panels, ceramic tile, or certain types of brick sealed with light-colored epoxy paint, or equivalent materials approved by the Health Department. Wall surfaces must extend eight (8) feet in height or to the ceiling if less than eight feet. Surfaces above paneling or tile must be light-colored, smooth, and washable.

Dry storage room walls must be taped and bedded sheetrock painted with light-colored epoxy or enamel paint to eight (8) feet, or use equivalent 
approved materials.

Toilet room walls must be FRP, ceramic tile, or certain types of brick sealed with epoxy paint to a minimum height of four (4) feet. Surfaces above must be light-colored, smooth, and cleanable.

Walls adjacent to the mop sink (if not in areas listed above) must have FRP or ceramic tile extending from floor to at least three (3) feet above the sink and on all sides.

Ceiling Requirements:

Ceilings in food preparation, customer service, tableware and utensil washing, mop sink, toilet rooms, and dry storage areas must be light-colored, smooth, relatively non-absorbent, and easily cleanable. Acceptable materials include vinyl-coated sheetrock panels, taped and bedded sheetrock with light-colored epoxy/enamel paint, or FRP panels.

Additional Requirements:

All restroom doors must have self-closing devices.
All restroom floors must have floor drains to allow proper drainage and cleaning.

attributes.NAME: MIRCH MASALA
attributes.VIOLATION_DESCRIPTION: Proper Cooling Time and Temperature
attributes.V_MEMO:
Observed improper cooling of multiple TCS food items, including yogurt, sauces, and broths. Product temperatures ranged from 50°F to 60°F and were stored in large, deep containers, preventing rapid heat transfer and proper cooling.

 Cool TCS foods from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F within an additional 4 hours (6 hours total). Large, deep containers do not allow foods to cool rapidly enough and increase the risk of bacterial growth.



Cooling tips: 
*

Divide food into smaller, shallow pans (2-4 inches deep).
*
Leave containers uncovered or loosely covered until food reaches 41°F.
*
Place pans in the walk-in cooler with space between them to allow air circulation.
*
Use ice baths or ice wands for soups, sauces, and broths.
*
Stir liquid foods frequently during cooling to release heat.
*
Do not stack cooling containers, and avoid placing large volumes of hot food directly into deep buckets or containers.
*
Monitor and document temperatures to verify the food reaches 70°F within 2 hours and 41°F within 6 hours.

attributes.NAME: MIRCH MASALA

Additional TCS foods, including raw chicken, cooked chicken, vegetables, and other raw and cooked items in the walk-in cooler, were observed between 46°F and 57°F.

Maintain all TCS foods requiring cold holding at 41°F or below. Do not store TCS foods in refrigeration equipment that cannot consistently maintain 41°F or below. Immediately repair or replace malfunctioning refrigeration equipment and evaluate all affected food for proper disposition in accordance with the Texas Food Establishment Rules.

Limit the amount of TCS food removed from temperature control to only the quantity that can be actively prepared within a short period of time. attributes.V_MEMO:

Additionally, fermented yogurt was observed at temperatures ranging from the 60s to 70s°F, indicating inadequate temperature control during the process.

Fermentation of TCS foods is a specialized food process requiring documented controls. The establishment shall submit written procedures outlining the fermentation process, including time and temperature monitoring, cooling procedures, and corrective actions. If safe control of the process cannot be demonstrated, an approved variance and HACCP plan may be required. Failure to properly control this process presents a risk for pathogen growth.

Until adequate documentation and process controls are implemented, discontinue yogurt fermentation or obtain approval for a variance/HACCP plan prior to resuming the process. Additionally, ensure fermented yogurt is properly cooled and maintained at 41°F or below once the fermentation process is complete.

attributes.NAME: CARMEN'S TACOS AND GORDITAS
attributes.VIOLATION_DESCRIPTION: Proper Cooling Time and Temperature
attributes.V_MEMO:
Observed beans prepared/cooked the previous day at approximately 52°F-59°F. The product had not cooled to 41°F or below within the required cooling timeframe and was discarded. TCS foods must be cooled from 135°F to 70°F within the first 2 hours, and then from 70°F to 41°F or below within the next 4 hours. Establish and follow a proper cooling procedure and actively monitor both time and temperature throughout the cooling process.

It is recommended that foods being cooled be labeled with a time stamp showing when cooling began so employees can properly track the required cooling timeframes. Monitor temperatures throughout the process to ensure the food reaches 70°F within the first 2 hours and 41°F or below within the following 4 hours.



Español: Se observaron frijoles preparados/cocinados el día anterior a aproximadamente 52°F-59°F. El producto no alcanzó 41°F o menos dentro del tiempo requerido de enfriamiento y fue desechado. Los alimentos TCS deben enfriarse de 135°F a 70°F dentro de las primeras 2 horas, y después de 70°F a 41°F o menos dentro de las siguientes 4 horas. Establecer y seguir un procedimiento adecuado de enfriamiento y monitorear activamente tanto el tiempo como la temperatura durante todo el proceso.

Se recomienda colocar una etiqueta con la hora (time stamp) indicando cuándo comenzó el proceso de enfriamiento para que los empleados puedan controlar correctamente los tiempos requeridos. Monitorear las temperaturas durante el proceso para asegurar que el alimento llegue a 70°F dentro de las primeras 2 horas y a 41°F o menos dentro de las siguientes 4 horas.

Have the dishmachine and chemical dispensing system properly evaluated and serviced/repaired as necessary to identify and correct the underlying issue. Al revisar documentación de inspecciones anteriores, se observó que este mismo problema con el suministro de desinfectante ya había ocurrido anteriormente. La máquina lavavajillas y el sistema dispensador de químicos deben ser evaluados adecuadamente y recibir servicio/reparación según sea necesario para identificar y corregir la causa del problema.
